analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, all supplied patches, the complete new changelog and CLI reference BASE excerpts (lines 1–787). These units contain documentation, not executable implementation; no concrete security regression is established. docs/provider/cli-reference.md HEAD 1078, 1094–1109 and 1117–1132 describe repeatable work-disk arguments, mounted APFS/ownership checks, interactive drive selection and an explicit-consent sudo ownership operation. HEAD 1249–1258 documents fail-closed planning with explicit disks; HEAD 1335 adds disk status rendering. changelog.d/sandbox-setup-work-disks.md:3–8 agrees with those contracts. The TLS-only installer trust limitation remains explicitly documented rather than newly introduced (TB-013, T-061, A-019).
Integration must examine SandboxWorkDisk.swift, SandboxCommand.swift and SandboxInstaller.swift changes to verify argument-safe subprocess invocation, mount/path validation across check-to-install transitions, consent and foreground handling for sudo, and refusal behavior on unsupported installers or failed disk plans. External VM/job storage and volume-wide ownership changes expand the CLI's local-storage and privilege surface; reconcile that behavior with TB-013/A-019 and provider availability interactions under TB-012/A-018. Actual add-on storage protections are an external contract, not an observed missing control here. T-041's encrypted inference-cache rules concern a separate storage subsystem: these documents do not establish that VM disks contain inference cache data or change its encryption, scope, TTL or keys. No supplied change alters attestation, serving authorization, token custody, billing or coordinator encryption. Implementation evidence is needed before resolving the work-disk and sudo security conclusions.
